Restore a Stelae snapshot

Usage: dolos bootstrap stelae [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --force
          Replace any data already in storage
      --source <SOURCE>
          Where to restore from, as a URL: `file://DIR` naming a stele directory, or
          `oci://HOST/PATH` naming a repository in a registry. Defaults to the configured network's
          official repository, and is required for a custom network
      --point <POINT>
          which stele in the repository to restore: `latest`, or `epoch-N` for the stele published
          at the end of epoch N. Registry sources only [default: latest]
      --skip-if-data
          Exit 0 without bootstrapping when storage already holds a node, as an interrupted replay
          that has committed leaves one for `--continue` to resume; data without one, as a bootstrap
          interrupted before it commits a cursor leaves, and a store this release refuses are errors
          instead
      --insecure
          talk to the repository over plaintext HTTP rather than HTTPS; for a registry on a loopback
          address or a mirror inside a cluster, and for nothing reachable from outside one
      --verbose
          Enable verbose logging output
      --scratch-dir <DIR>
          directory to stage pulled layers in; defaults to `<storage.path>/scratch`. registry
          sources only — a `file://` restore stages nothing
      --skip-space-check
          skip the restore disk-space preflight and continue even when the stele's declared sizes
          exceed the available space
      --registry-user <USER>
          the user to read the registry as; defaults to the published read-only user when the
          repository is the configured network's official one. The password comes from
          DOLOS_STELAE_PASSWORD or --registry-credentials-file [env: DOLOS_STELAE_USER=]
      --registry-credentials-file <PATH>
          a TOML file naming the registry secret as `password` or `token`; it takes the place of
          DOLOS_STELAE_PASSWORD / DOLOS_STELAE_TOKEN
  -c, --config <CONFIG>
          
  -h, --help
          Print help
